quotes.text: Learn how to use Stripe Tax to calculate and collect taxes in your custom integration with Elements.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: This is a Checkout Sessions API for when api-integration is checkout.
This is a Payment Intents API for when api-integration is elements.
Stripe offers two ways to handle tax in custom payment flows. Choose based on how much control you need over tax reversals:
Stripe Tax only calculates tax in jurisdictions where you’re registered to collect tax.
The Tax API doesn’t automatically validate tax IDs against government databases.

findings: Semantic delta: the 2026-11-07 capture is a 14-line index with only a general purpose statement and two variant URLs (new raw lines 1-14); the diff replaces the older detailed body with index navigation (diff lines 1-16, 2597-2601). It does not itself establish changed tax behavior, beta status, deprecation, or current variant content.

Baseline summary error independent of the new capture: source-stripe-checkout-collect-taxes.md lines 13 and 86 imply the Payment Intents path uses only the full Tax API; old raw lines 553-559 explicitly present two choices, a Payment Intents integration with automatic transaction/reversal handling and flat-amount reversals, or custom Tax API for line-item reversals, multiple processors, and recording control.

Baseline count error independent of the new capture: source-stripe-checkout-collect-taxes.md lines 138-143 and stripe-tax.md line 120 say 100+ types across 100+ countries. The old raw's country/type tables at lines 431-545 and 2445-2559 enumerate 107 country/type rows, 96 distinct country codes, and 80 distinct enum types; there is no stated 100+ countries or 100+ distinct types in that captured evidence.

The existing source has only the April raw in frontmatter and Raw Sources (source lines 4-8, 157-159). A source update should retain that dated detailed provenance and link the November variant index separately, with navigation-only labeling; the new raw lines 11-14 do not verify either variant body's current behavior.

Historical operational qualifications remain in the old capture: registrations before tax calculation (old raw lines 568-570), Checkout automatic_tax/tax_code/tax_behavior and UI-mode-specific address behavior (old raw lines 16-24, 64-117), Tax API calculation versus subsequent transaction recording and reversal (old raw lines 879-898, 931-1040), and testing limitations (old raw lines 1415-1425).

Baseline validation error independent of November: source-stripe-checkout-collect-taxes.md lines 145-148 say asynchronous government checks are 'always' after the custom Tax API discussion, without an API-path qualifier. In the April Checkout Sessions Tax ID Element flow, only format is checked during the Session and government checks for AU ABN/EU VAT/GB VAT follow asynchronously (old raw lines 408-416); the Payment Intents Tax ID Element flow says likewise during payment/setup confirmation (old raw lines 2424-2430). By contrast, custom Tax API calculation with customer_details.tax_ids can reject invalid format but does not automatically check government databases (old raw lines 1633-1681).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the April 21, 2026 Checkout Sessions custom Elements automatic-tax path, including tax code/behavior, conditional address collection and shipping-address priority, as dated guidance (old raw lines 12-117; source lines 17-46).

Retain the April 21, 2026 custom Tax API calculation, PaymentIntent amount/metadata, post-payment tax transaction, full/partial reversals, 90-day calculation expiration, 30 partial-reversal limit, and proportional-refund reporting caveat as dated guidance (old raw lines 547-559, 848-898, 1036-1040, 1126-1133, 1486-1541).

Retain path-specific dated Tax ID Element preview/beta flags and state boundaries: Checkout custom_checkout_tax_id_1 and custom_checkout_tax_id_verification_1 (old raw lines 306-321, 414-429); Payment Intents elements_tax_id_1 and elements_tax_id_verification_1, optional CustomerSession for save/redisplay, and confirmation/async validation distinctions (old raw lines 2249-2271, 2312-2336, 2393-2430). Government checks in these dated Tax ID Element flows must remain separate from custom Tax API calculation, which checks format but does not automatically validate tax IDs against government databases (old raw lines 1667-1681).
conflicts: The current source's unqualified PI-only-Tax-API framing (source lines 13, 86) conflicts with the old guide's explicit two-option comparison (old raw lines 553-559); add a narrow correction rather than attributing it to November.

The source and stripe-tax concept's 100+ country/type claims (source lines 138-143; concept line 120) are unsupported by the enumerated April tables (old raw lines 431-545, 2445-2559); make coverage dated and distinguish rows, country codes, and enum types.

The new variant index cannot resolve the current preview/flag status of Tax ID Element or current API behavior, although source lines 60-84 and 145-148 describe older preview details (new raw lines 9-14; old raw lines 306-321, 414-429, 2249-2265, 2428-2443).

The source's unqualified 'Async (always)' wording at lines 145-148 conflates dated Tax ID Element government checks with custom Tax API tax-ID input. The April guide attaches asynchronous AU ABN/EU VAT/GB VAT checks to Checkout Session and Payment/Setup confirmation (old raw lines 408-416, 2424-2430), but says custom Tax API calculations reject malformed IDs and do not automatically validate against government databases (old raw lines 1667-1681). This is a pre-existing summary conflict, not a November change.
unresolved_questions: The two linked 2026-11-07 variant bodies were not part of the pinned packet and were not fetched; their current functional text, beta status, and API-version qualifiers remain unverified (new raw lines 11-14).

findings: Add navigation-only November raw provenance without replacing the April guide (source lines 4-8, 157-159; new raw lines 9-14). Correct the pre-existing PI-only Tax API framing (source lines 13, 86; old raw lines 553-559), unsupported 100+ country/type counts (source lines 138-143; old raw lines 431-545, 2445-2559), and unqualified 'Async (always)' government-validation claim (source lines 145-148; old raw lines 408-416, 1667-1681, 2424-2430). The source's validation section can mislead a custom Tax API integrator about a government check that does not occur (source lines 145-148; old raw lines 1667-1681).
source_assessments.reason: A bounded source correction is needed for baseline accuracy and provenance, while the semantic raw delta is navigation only.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/tax, the complete November capture only identifies Stripe Tax for custom Elements integrations and routes to Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents variants (new raw lines 5-14); it establishes no current calculation, collection, payment-success, or beta-state contract. The April capture supplies dated detail: Checkout Sessions enables automatic_tax with tax classification and behavior (old raw lines 16-24), whereas the Payment Intents section distinguishes automatic tax handling from the custom Tax API for calculation, separate transaction recording, and reversals, subject to registration and payment-state timing (old raw lines 547-570, 879-898). The mapped source-stripe-checkout-collect-taxes.md retains both paths but incorrectly frames Payment Intents as only the full Tax API (source lines 11-13, 86), overstates its table counts (source lines 138-143), and leaves its 'Async (always)' government-check claim unqualified (source lines 145-148). The old Tax ID Element flows describe later AU ABN/EU VAT/GB VAT checks, while custom Tax API tax-ID input only gets format checking and no automatic government-database validation (old raw lines 408-416, 1667-1681, 2424-2430).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/tax, the November delta is presentation and variant navigation, not a proven substantive functional change (new raw lines 9-14; old raw lines 8-10, 547-559). Preserve the April behavior as dated in source-stripe-checkout-collect-taxes.md: Checkout Sessions Elements address and tax-ID preview rules, the alternative Payment Intents versus custom Tax API choice, separate payment/calculation/recording states, and refund reversal limits (old raw lines 64-117, 306-321, 879-898, 1036-1040). Correct that summary's PI-only framing, unsupported 100+ country/type statement, and unqualified 'Async (always)' government-check assertion (source lines 13, 138-148; old raw lines 431-545, 408-416, 1667-1681, 2424-2430). Government checks in the dated Tax ID Element flows are distinct from Tax API calculation, which checks tax-ID format without automatic database validation. New links do not establish current beta flags, client/server steps, tax-law correctness, completed payment, or the contents of the variant bodies.
